new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work was listed (Foley 1986), already marked silent and checked above with 15 additional full-text queries; nothing on stress was missed. Spot-checks of the other files in the directory (not listed works): APiCS survey 69 text (Foley 2013, sister pidgin yima1244) mentions only a phrase-level falling pitch on clause-final verbs (lines 1101-1106), no word stress; the Williams 2000 p. 37 preview scanned has no stress/accent/phonology terms.

sources.note: Bibliographic record only: two references, Glottolog's most extensive description = Williams 2000 (grammar sketch, 26 pp.) and Williams 1993 (a wordlist or less, 2 pp.).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2013. Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin (survey chapter 69). In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds.), The Survey of Pidgin and Creole Languages, vol. III / APiCS Online.https://apics-online.info/surveys/69
sources.note: Describes the sister pidgin (yima1244), not the target; mentions Yimas-Alamblak Pidgin only as 'quite different from the Yimas pidgin used to trading partners speaking Alamblak (Williams 2000)'. Its phonology section gives segments only; no stress/accent statement for any Yimas-based pidgin (only a phrase-level falling-pitch remark on clause chaining in sec. 8).

sources.citation: Williams, Jeffrey P. 2000. Yimas-Alamblak Tanim Tok: an indigenous trade pidgin of New Guinea. Journal of Pidgin and Creole Languages 15(1): 37-62.
